extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / beginning graduate students studying complex analysis (conformal mappings and elliptic functions)
extracted.subtask_description: Work through and prove the listed exercises and problems on conformal mappings, the Schwarz-Pick lemma, automorphisms of the disc/half-plane, elliptic integrals, and the basic construction/theorems for elliptic functions (Weierstrass ℘). Each rubric entry below corresponds to a theorem, lemma, definition, exercise, or problem statement that a student is expected to establish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 1: local bijection <=> nonvanishing derivative
rubrics_metrics.description: A holomorphic mapping f : U → V is a local bijection on U (for every z ∈ U there exists an open disc D ⊂ U centered at z so that f : D → f(D) is a bijection) if and only if f'(z) ≠ 0 for all z ∈ U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use Rouché’s theorem as in the proof of Proposition 1.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 2: local structure at a double zero; orthogonal curves
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose F is holomorphic near z0 with F(z0) = F'(z0) = 0 and F''(z0) ≠ 0. Show there are two curves Γ1 and Γ2 through z0, orthogonal at z0, such that F restricted to Γ1 is real with a minimum at z0 and F restricted to Γ2 is real with a maximum at z0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Write F(z) = g(z)^2 near z0, consider z ↦ g(z) and its inverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 3: conformal equivalence preserves simple connectedness
rubrics_metrics.description: If U and V are conformally equivalent, prove that if U is simply connected then so is V. The conclusion remains valid if there exists merely a continuous bijection between U and V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4: existence of holomorphic surjection from unit disc to C
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether there exists a holomorphic surjection from the unit disc to C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Move the upper half-plane 'down' and then square it to get C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 5: conformal map from half-disc to upper half-plane
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that f(z) = -1/2 (z + 1/z) is a conformal map from the half-disc {z : |z| < 1, y > 0} to the upper half-plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Solve f(z) = w leads to quadratic z^2 + 2wz + 1 = 0; for w in H the roots are distinct and give the inverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 6: Laplacian under composition with holomorphic map
rubrics_metrics.description: Give another proof of Lemma 1.3 by showing directly that the Laplacian of u ◦ F is zero when F is holomorphic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use the Cauchy-Riemann equations for the real and imaginary parts of F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 7: details of Dirichlet solution in a strip
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide full details for the formula solving the Dirichlet problem in a strip; compute the solution at z = i y for 0 < y < 1, derive expressions for r, θ and the Poisson kernel integrals, change variables t = (1/π) log((i - e^{iϕ})/(i + e^{iϕ})), and deduce the integral identities given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the subparts (a)-(c): compute reiθ = G(iy), deduce r^2 and Pr(θ-ϕ) formulas; change variables to t, use identities sinϕ = 1/cosh πt and dϕ/dt = π / cosh πt, then transform the integrals accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 8: harmonic function in first quadrant with specified boundary values
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a harmonic function u in the open first quadrant, continuous up to the boundary except at 0 and 1, that equals 1 on the rays {y=0, x>1} and {x=0, y>0} and equals 0 on the segment {0<x<1, y=0}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Find successive conformal maps F1,...,F5 as indicated in Figure 11; use u = (1/π) arg(z) on H, which equals 0 on positive real axis and 1 on negative real axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 9: harmonic function u = Re((i+z)/(i-z)) in unit disc
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove u(z) = Re((i+z)/(i-z)) is harmonic in the unit disc, vanishes on its boundary, and u(0,1) = 0; note u is not bounded in D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 10: Schwarz-type bound for holomorphic F : H→C with |F|≤1 and F(i)=0
rubrics_metrics.description: Let F : H → C be holomorphic, |F(z)| ≤ 1 and F(i) = 0. Prove |F(z)| ≤ |(z - i)/(z + i)| for all z ∈ H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 11: Schwarz-lemma style inequality on disc
rubrics_metrics.description: If f : D(0,R) → C is holomorphic with |f(z)| ≤ M, then show (f(z) - f(0)) / (M^2 - f(0) f(z)) ≤ |z|/(M R) (as given in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use the Schwarz lemma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 12: fixed points of holomorphic self-maps of D
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If f : D → D is analytic and has two distinct fixed points then f is the identity. (b) Must every holomorphic f : D → D have a fixed point? (Consider upper half-plane.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 13: pseudo-hyperbolic distance and Schwarz-Pick
rubrics_metrics.description: Define ρ(z,w) = |(z - w)/(1 -  w z)| (pseudo-hyperbolic). (a) Prove that for holomorphic f : D → D, ρ(f(z), f(w)) ≤ ρ(z,w) for all z,w, and equality holds for automorphisms. (b) Prove |f'(z)|/(1 - |f(z)|^2) ≤ 1/(1 - |z|^2) for all z (Schwarz-Pick lemma).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use automorphisms ψ_α(z) = (z - α)/(1 -  α z) and apply the Schwarz lemma to ψ_{f(w)} ◦ f ◦ ψ_w^{-1}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 14: form of conformal maps H→D
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that all conformal mappings from the upper half-plane H to the unit disc D take the form e^{iθ} (z - β)/(z -  β), with θ ∈ R and β ∈ H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 15: automorphisms of H with fixed real points and interpolation
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If Φ is an automorphism of H that fixes three distinct points on the real axis then Φ is the identity. (b) Given two ordered triples (x1<x2<x3) and (y1<y2<y3) of distinct real points, prove there exists a unique automorphism Φ of H with Φ(x_j)=y_j (and similarly for other cyclic orders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 16: Möbius matrices representing automorphisms via f and ψ_α
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f(z) = (i - z)/(i + z) and its inverse f^{-1}. (a) Given θ ∈ R find real a,b,c,d with ad-bc=1 such that f^{-1}(e^{iθ} f(z)) = (az+b)/(cz+d) for z ∈ H. (b) Given α ∈ D find real a,b,c,d with ad-bc=1 so that (az+b)/(cz+d) = f^{-1}(ψ_α(f(z))). (c) Prove any automorphism g of the unit disc is conjugate to such a real matrix form via f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use parts (a) and (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 17: integrals of ψ_α and area computations
rubrics_metrics.description: For ψ_α(z) = (α - z)/(1 -  α z) with |α|<1, prove ∫_D (1/π) |ψ'_α|^2 dx dy = 1 and ∫_D (1/π) |ψ'_α| dx dy = (1 - |α|^2)/|α|^2 log(1/(1 - |α|^2)) (with the α=0 limiting interpretation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: First integral can be evaluated without calculation. For second use polar coordinates and contour integration in θ for fixed r.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 18: boundary extension of conformal map to piecewise-smooth polygonal boundary
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose Ω is a simply connected domain bounded by a piecewise-smooth closed curve γ. Then any conformal map F of D to Ω extends to a continuous bijection of the closed disc D to closure(Ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof generalizes the argument used in Theorem 4.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 19: simply connectedness of plane slit along rays union
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that the complex plane slit along the union ∪_{k=1}^n {A_k + i y : y ≤ 0} (a finite union of downward vertical rays) is simply connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Given a curve, first 'raise' it into the upper half-plane so it avoids the slits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 20: elliptic integrals mapping H to rectangles
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) The integral ∫_0^z dζ/[ζ(ζ-1)(ζ-λ)]^{1/2} with λ ∈ R, λ ≠ 1 maps the upper half-plane conformally to a rectangle (one vertex is the image of ∞). (b) For λ=-1, the integral maps to a square whose side-lengths are Γ(1/4)^2/(2√(2π)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 21: Schwarz-Christoffel maps to triangles
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Show ∫_0^z ζ^{-β1} (1 - ζ)^{-β2} dζ maps H to a triangle with vertices images of 0,1,∞ and interior angles α_j π where α_j + β_j = 1 and β1 + β2 + β3 = 2, for 0<β1,β2<1 and 1<β1+β2<2. (b)-(c) Analyze cases β1+β2=1 and 0<β1+β2<1. (d) Provide formula for side-length opposite α_j.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 22: Schwarz-Christoffel map for polygon boundary
rubrics_metrics.description: If P is a simply connected polygon with vertices a1,...,an and angles α1π,...,αnπ and F is a conformal map of D to P, then there exist unit-modulus complex numbers B1,...,Bn and constants c1,c2 so that F(z) = c1 ∫_0^z dζ / (ζ - B1)^{β1} ··· (ζ - Bn)^{βn} + c2, with β_j = 1 - α_j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use correspondence between H and D and a similar argument to Theorem 4.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 23: mapping D onto regular polygon via integral
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that F(z) = ∫_0^z dζ/(1 - ζ^n)^{2/n} maps the unit disc conformally onto the interior of a regular n-gon and compute its perimeter via an integral involving (sin θ)^{-2/n}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 24: identities for elliptic integrals K and K'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: change variables in the integrals as indicated in text; relate to hypergeometric integral representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems 1: isogonality, isotropy and holomorphic derivative condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f be C^1 near z0. Define isogonal and isotropic at z0 and show f is isogonal iff isotropic. Prove f is isogonal at z0 iff f'(z0) exists and is nonzero, or that holds for conjugate f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems 2: oriented angle between complex numbers and angle preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Define the oriented angle between complex numbers z and w via inner products; (b) For smooth curves γ and η intersecting at z0, define angle via tangents; (c) Prove if f is holomorphic and f'(z0) ≠ 0 then f preserves angles at z0; (d) Conversely, if f is real-differentiable at z0 with nonzero Jacobian and preserves angles then f is holomorphic at z0 with f'(z0) ≠ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints given: use formula (f'(z0)γ'(t0), f'(z0)η'(t0)) = |f'(z0)|^2 (γ'(t0), η'(t0)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems 3: hyperbolic (Poincaré) metric and Schwarz-Pick consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Define hyperbolic length |w|_z = |w|/(1-|z|^2) and hyperbolic distance via infimum of integrals; use Schwarz-Pick to show holomorphic f : D→D is distance-decreasing in this metric. (b) Automorphisms of D preserve hyperbolic distance; conversely preserving maps are automorphisms (up to conjugation). (c)-(e) Show existence of automorphism sending z1→0 and z2→s∈[0,1), compute d(0,s) = (1/2) log((1+s)/(1-s)), and find formula for hyperbolic distance between any two points in D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems 4: SU(1,1) matrix group and automorphisms of the disc
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Prove matrices preserving the hermitian form z1 w1 - z2 w2 with determinant 1 are of form [[a, b],[b, a]] with |a|^2 - |b|^2 = 1. (b) Show SU(1,1)/{±1} is isomorphic to the group of automorphisms of D via the association between matrices and fractional linear maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use matrix J = [[0,1],[0,-1]] and the given association e^{2iθ}(z-α)/(1-α z) ↔ explicit matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems 5: bounded holomorphic functions on H with zeros on imaginary axis
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If F : H→C is holomorphic and bounded, vanishing at z = i r_n for a bounded positive sequence {r_n} with ∑ r_n = ∞, then F ≡ 0. (b) If ∑ r_n < ∞ it is possible to construct a bounded function on H with zeros precisely at i r_n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related results in unit disc referenced (Chapter 5 problems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems 6: Carathéodory extension (closed continuous simple γ)
rubrics_metrics.description: The results of Exercise 18 extend to the case when γ is merely closed, simple, and continuous (proof requires further ideas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems 7: Koebe's proof strategy and expansions for Riemann mapping theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline Koebe's iterative method: starting from a Koebe domain K0 ⊂ D (simply connected, proper subset containing 0) construct expansions f_n so K_{n+1}=f_n(K_n) enlarges domain; define inner radius r_K and expansions (holomorphic injections with f(0)=0 and |f(z)|>|z|) and prove properties: expansions increase r_K, |f'(0)|>1, the sequence F_n is an expansion and |F_n'(0)| increases to 1, osculating sequences converge to conformal map F:K0→D. Construct expansions using automorphisms ψ_α and square-root S on K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parts (a)-(e) give precise steps; hints include writing f(z)=z g(z) and using Schwarz lemma and choosing α on boundary with |α|=r_K and β^2=α.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems 8: Bieberbach coefficient bounds when coefficients real
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f injective holomorphic in D with f(0)=0 and f'(0)=1 and real coefficients f(z)=z + a2 z^2 + ... Show |a2| ≤ 2 and outline proof that |a_n| ≤ n when coefficients are real (parts a-f), culminating with the extremal example f(z)=z/(1-z)^2 having |a_n|=n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Fourier coefficients of imaginary part on circle, bounds |sin nθ| ≤ n sin θ, symmetry to real axis, small-r asymptotics, and letting r→1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems 9: arithmetic-geometric mean and connection to elliptic integrals
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Show iterations of arithmetic and geometric mean sequences {a_n},{b_n} converge to common limit M(a,b). (b) Prove Gauss's identity 1/M(a,b) = (2/π) ∫_0^{π/2} dθ / (a^2 cos^2 θ + b^2 sin^2 θ)^{1/2} by showing invariance I(a,b) = I((a+b)/2,√(ab)) and relate I(a,b) to K(k) with k^2 = 1 - b^2/a^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use monotonicity and difference bounds for sequences; relate integral to K(k) and use Exercise 24 identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 1.1: fundamental parallelogram and lattice coverage properties
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is meromorphic with periods 1 and τ generating lattice Λ, then (i) every point in C is congruent to a unique point in fundamental parallelogram P0, (ii) same for any period parallelogram P0 + h, (iii) Λ provides a disjoint covering C = ∪_{n,m} (n + mτ + P0), (iv) f is completely determined by its values in any period parallelogram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses basis property of 1 and τ over R and integer translation to place any z in P0 uniquely; uniqueness by range constraints 0≤a<1,0≤b<1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 1.2: entire doubly periodic functions are constant
rubrics_metrics.description: An entire doubly periodic function is constant because it is bounded on C (determined by values on compact closure of P0) and Liouville's theorem applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 1.3: elliptic functions have at least two poles in P0
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonconstant elliptic (doubly periodic meromorphic) function must have at least two poles in the fundamental parallelogram P0 (counting multiplicity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: use residue theorem on ∂P0 and periodicity to show integral of f around boundary is 0, so total residue is 0, hence there can't be a single simple pole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 1.4: number of zeros equals number of poles (order) in P0
rubrics_metrics.description: Every elliptic function of order m has exactly m zeros in P0 (counted with multiplicity); equivalently the number of zeros equals the number of poles in P0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: apply the argument principle to f'/f on ∂P0 and use periodicity to show integral is 0 so Nz = Np.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1.5: double series convergence for lattice sums when r>2
rubrics_metrics.description: The double series ∑_{(n,m)≠(0,0)} 1/(|n|+|m|)^r and ∑_{n+mτ∈Λ*} 1/|n + mτ|^r converge when r>2; equivalently the lattice zeta-type series converges absolutely for r>2 (uniformly on Im τ ≥ δ>0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketched via summation in m then n, integral comparison, and estimate |n|+|m| ≲ |n + mτ| when τ ∈ H; remark that r=2 fails to converge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/Construction: Weierstrass ℘ function
rubrics_metrics.description: Define ℘(z) = 1/z^2 + ∑_{ω∈Λ*} (1/(z+ω)^2 - 1/ω^2). This series converges (by Lemma 1.5) and defines a meromorphic function with double poles at lattice points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convergence handled by splitting sum over |ω|≤2R and |ω|>2R to show tail is O(1/|ω|^3) uniformly on compact sets; subtraction of 1/ω^2 ensures absolute convergence of terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 1.6: ℘ is elliptic of order two and ℘' series
rubrics_metrics.description: The Weierstrass ℘ function is elliptic with periods 1 and τ and has double poles at lattice points. Its derivative is ℘'(z) = -2 ∑_{n,m} 1/(z + n + mτ)^3, which converges absolutely off lattice points and is clearly periodic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiation removes the -1/ω^2 subtraction so ℘' series is manifestly periodic with periods 1 and τ; evenness of ℘ (℘(z)=℘(-z)) then forces any additive constants from periodicity to be zero.
